_comment: Each entry names a security guard, a surgical edit that DISABLES it, and the
test(s) that must fail once it is disabled. The harness applies the edit, runs
the suite, asserts those named tests failed, and restores the file.
The point is the #916 lesson: a regression guard that still passes on buggy
code is worse than no guard, because it certifies the gap. A test only earns
its green when it has been seen to go red for the right reason.
Repo-level by design so any boundary can register here later (the guard trio,
secrets-guard). Registered today only for the #931 active-grant boundary — the
shape is general, the coverage is deliberately not.
Adding an entry: each edit's `find` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in `file`. Prefer disabling a
condition (`if (false && ...)`) over deleting a block, so the mutation stays
syntactically valid — a mutation that fails to COMPILE proves nothing, since
the suite would fail for the wrong reason. The harness checks the named tests
